solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Passing English pub by green? Days lost!

indicators.note: the days are lost: D, the abbreviation for day, is dropped from the green

blocks.note: PH = public house, the map abbreviation

explanation.surface: Someone walks past an English pub on the village green and wonders where the days went.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Passing' looks like a verb about walking by; it is the adjective meaning fleeting.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ephemeral is passing: it lasts only a short time.

clue.text: One who’s had cooler experience in City on receiving kiss?

indicators.note: City takes the kiss inside it

blocks.note: EC, the postcode of the City of London
X = a kiss, as at the end of a letter

explanation.surface: A question about someone's chillier experience in the City, on being kissed.
explanation.walkthrough: The cooler is slang for prison, so 'cooler experience' is time served, nothing to do with temperature.
explanation.definitionFit: An ex-con is a former convict, one who has done time in the cooler.

clue.text: Lead singers growl in this context

blocks.note: Pb, the dense grey element, not the front singer
the rock genre known for growled vocals

explanation.surface: A note that lead singers growl in this kind of setting.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Lead singers' as one phrase and you look for a band's frontmen; split it, and Lead is the metal Pb.
explanation.definitionFit: Lead is a dense metal, and heavy metal is also a loud rock genre with growled vocals.

clue.text: Mike slow to return after year working as henchman

indicators.note: the word for slow is turned back

blocks.note: Mike is M in the NATO alphabet
on = working, as a machine is

explanation.surface: Mike, sluggish about coming back after a year, is now employed as someone's heavy.
explanation.walkthrough: The Myrmidons were Achilles's loyal troops, so the word came to mean a follower who carries out orders without question.
explanation.definitionFit: A myrmidon is a hired follower who does the dirty work, which is a henchman.

clue.text: Mysterious force that was guarding territory it patrolled?

indicators.note: the old force surrounds the territory

blocks.note: the Royal Ulster Constabulary, a police force since replaced
NI = Northern Ireland, where the RUC policed

explanation.surface: A strange force that once guarded the ground it patrolled.
explanation.walkthrough: The RUC was Northern Ireland's police force until 2001, which is why the setter says 'that was'.
explanation.definitionFit: Runic means written in runes, hence mysterious or cryptic.

clue.text: Rule at sea revised for eminent poets

indicators.note: the letters are rewritten into a new order

explanation.surface: A maritime regulation gets rewritten for the benefit of famous poets.
explanation.walkthrough: A poet laureate is the official national poet, and the word also covers other honoured poets.
explanation.definitionFit: A laureate is one crowned with laurel for distinction, and the word is used above all of honoured poets.

clue.text: Drink in short time artist knocked back, like punch

indicators.note: the other pieces go inside the short time
the artist is turned backwards, as a drink is knocked back

blocks.note: to chin someone is to punch them on the chin

explanation.surface: Someone downs a quick drink that an artist knocks back, strong as punch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drink', 'knocked back' and 'punch' all belong to the bar, but punch is the verb to hit and knocked back just reverses RA.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by category: maraschino is a liqueur distilled from marasca cherries, one kind of drink.

clue.text: Scottish Thomas needs elevation when crossing over deep ditch

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising the word turns it upside down

blocks.note: Tam is the Scots form of Tom
O = over, as in cricket scoring

explanation.surface: A Scotsman called Thomas has to climb to get across a deep trench.
explanation.walkthrough: TAM around O gives TAOM, which the upward turn makes MOAT; 'when' just joins.
explanation.definitionFit: A moat is a deep, wide ditch around a castle.

clue.text: Right to replace the 50 leading multitude in sector

blocks.note: LEGION (a multitude) loses its leading L (50 in Roman numerals)

explanation.surface: A right to replace the fifty who lead a crowd in some area.
explanation.walkthrough: L is 50 in Roman numerals, and it is the letter leading LEGION.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: both words name a marked-off part of a larger area.

clue.text: Irresponsible broadcast about intelligence

indicators.note: the word for broadcast goes around the intelligence

explanation.surface: A careless broadcast on the subject of intelligence.
explanation.walkthrough: Broadcast is the farming sense, sowing seed by scattering it, not radio.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone scatterbrained is disorganised and forgetful, which the setter stretches to careless or irresponsible.

clue.text: Manhattan location: down there, son joins percussion section

blocks.note: the kitchen is slang for an orchestra's percussion section

explanation.surface: A New York address given as downstairs, where a son joins the drums.
explanation.walkthrough: Hell's Kitchen is a Manhattan neighbourhood; the orchestral 'kitchen' is the clatter of pots and pans at the back.
explanation.definitionFit: Hell's Kitchen is a district on the west side of Manhattan.

clue.text: Coming before Society, upstanding character’s entertained by unthinkable ideas

indicators.note: the character is held inside

blocks.note: I, the letter that stands as a single upright stroke

explanation.surface: Before a society meeting, an upright person indulges some unthinkable ideas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not on' is the British idiom for something unacceptable.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a notion is a conception held in the mind, an idea.

clue.text: Is one sly-looking gent with pipe, wayward old male?

definitions.text: Is one sly-looking gent with pipe, wayward old male?

indicators.note: the letters stray from their order

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a shifty old man with a pipe is up to no good.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes the answer as well as spelling it: a furtive old man with a wandering eye.
explanation.definitionFit: A peeping Tom is a man who secretly watches others, sly-looking and wayward.

clue.text: Found inside cake, note needing no decryption

indicators.note: the note is placed inside the cake

explanation.surface: A message baked into a cake that nobody needs to decode.
explanation.walkthrough: Note is not a musical letter here but the abbreviation n., since no musical note gives N.
explanation.definitionFit: En clair is French for 'in the clear': sent as plain text, needing no decryption.

clue.text: Pain where one probes abnormal lung area

indicators.note: one goes into the rearranged letters
the letters of lung area are put in an irregular order

explanation.surface: A doctor locates pain where a probe explores an unhealthy part of the lung.
explanation.walkthrough: The medical surface makes 'lung area' read as anatomy; it is just the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Neuralgia is sharp pain along a nerve.

clue.text: Stop the Alsatian chasing sheep? On the contrary!

indicators.note: to chase is to follow behind, so one piece comes after the other

explanation.surface: A plea to call off the Alsatian dog that is chasing the sheep.
explanation.walkthrough: The Alsatian looks like the dog; it is a person from Alsace, where French is spoken. 'On the contrary' flips who chases whom, so the sheep follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a let-up is a pause or cessation, as in 'the rain showed no let-up'.

clue.text: Waste of time without beer? Get round in!

definitions.note: adjective: 'it's a waste of time' is 'it's pointless'

indicators.note: 'get round in' means bring the round inside, as you would bring washing in

explanation.surface: A drinker complains that a night with no beer is wasted, and demands someone buy a round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get round in' sounds like buying the drinks; it tells you to put the round letter O inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: calling something a waste of time is calling it pointless, having no purpose.

clue.text: Mean sort most petty of thieves?

blocks.note: read literally, one who pinches (steals) only pennies

explanation.surface: Asking whether the stingiest person is also the pettiest thief.
explanation.walkthrough: Pinch is British slang for steal, so a penny-pincher read literally steals tiny sums.
explanation.definitionFit: Mean in the British sense of stingy: someone who counts every coin, and read literally a thief of coppers.

clue.text: Italian educator most senior going to pieces

indicators.note: the words break up and are reassembled

explanation.surface: An elderly Italian teacher, the most senior on the staff, is falling apart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Going to pieces' fits the ageing-teacher picture, but it only tells you to break up 'most senior'.
explanation.definitionFit: Maria Montessori was the Italian educator behind the Montessori method.

clue.text: Memorial of significance featuring Greek character

indicators.note: the significance has the Greek letter inside it

explanation.surface: An important memorial carries a Greek inscription.
explanation.walkthrough: Moment in the old sense of importance, as in 'a matter of great moment'.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: both are structures built to commemorate a person or event.

clue.text: An environmental problem we hear?

blocks.note: reads as smog or litter, dirt in the air or water
seems to mean 'so we are told'; really, it reaches us through our ears

explanation.surface: A news item about an environmental issue that people are talking about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'We hear' seems to mean 'we are told'; the problem is one you literally hear.
explanation.definitionFit: Pollution usually means dirt in air or water, but excessive sound is also officially classed as an environmental pollutant.

clue.text: Washed out: I considered ringing doctor

indicators.note: considered forms a ring around doctor

explanation.surface: Someone, feeling drained, thought about phoning the doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: Doctor is the verb to tamper with, not a physician, and ringing is not a phone call.
explanation.definitionFit: Medical sense: a surgeon irrigates a wound by flushing it with liquid, which is washing it out.

clue.text: No editor — and no editorial?

blocks.note: a leader is a newspaper editorial

explanation.surface: A newspaper with no editor and no opinion column.
explanation.walkthrough: In British papers the leader is the editorial column, so a leaderless paper also lacks its editorial.
explanation.definitionFit: Leaderless means having no one in charge, as a paper without its editor.

clue.text: Railway Children like TV after school

explanation.surface: The Railway Children enjoy watching television after lessons.
explanation.walkthrough: The Railway Children is a classic children's novel, but here the words split: a toy railway that children like.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by description: the novel's title is split so it describes a toy railway that children like.

clue.text: Some stiffness evident in this colonel with rat given whipping

indicators.note: the letters are beaten into a new order

explanation.surface: A stiff colonel stands by while a rat is thrashed.
explanation.walkthrough: An Eton collar is the broad stiff white collar once worn by Eton College boys, a school where whipping was once routine.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by description: the broad starched collar was notoriously rigid, so stiffness is literally on show in it.

clue.text: Black material and brown material?

explanation.surface: Two fabrics, one black and one brown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Black material and brown material' looks like two definitions; black material is TAR and 'brown' alone is TAN, leaving the last 'material' as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by category: this checked woollen cloth of the Scottish clans is one kind of material.

clue.text: You could pick this pair of idiots in pub around university

indicators.note: the idiots go inside the pub
the second idiot goes around the university

blocks.note: two fools, an ass and a git, with the U going inside the second

explanation.surface: You might choose these two fools drinking in a pub near the university.
explanation.walkthrough: Pick is plucking strings with a plectrum, not choosing. A git is British slang for a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: A bass guitar is played by picking the strings.

clue.text: Long for introduction from Ricetti to enter grotto

indicators.note: an introduction is what comes first, so only Ricetti's opening letter is used
that letter goes into the grotto

explanation.surface: Someone longing for a word from a man called Ricetti as he enters a grotto.
explanation.walkthrough: Ricetti is a made-up name, there only to supply its initial.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: both mean to want something intensely.

clue.text: Excitement? Yours truly’s in a state!

indicators.note: the setter's I'M goes inside

explanation.surface: The setter admits to being worked up and flustered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In a state' is the idiom for agitated, but here it is literal: I'M inside A NATION.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: animation is liveliness and excitement, as in 'she spoke with animation'.

clue.text: Occasion for wreath-laying made mercenary angry with bishop

indicators.note: the letters are stirred up

explanation.surface: At a ceremony a hired soldier is angered by a bishop.
explanation.walkthrough: Remembrance Day, 11 November, is when Britain and the Commonwealth lay wreaths for the war dead.
explanation.definitionFit: Remembrance Day is marked by laying wreaths at war memorials.

clue.text: Spelling master in revolutionary English school

indicators.note: the letters revolve, turning back to front

blocks.note: a gam is a school of whales

explanation.surface: A spelling teacher works at a radical English school.
explanation.walkthrough: Spelling is casting spells, not orthography, so the master is a magician.
explanation.definitionFit: Spelling is read as casting spells, and a mage is an old word for a magician.

clue.text: Two notes interrupting calm musical piece

indicators.note: the notes break into the word for calm

blocks.note: A and D, two notes of the scale

explanation.surface: A couple of notes break into a quiet piece of music.
explanation.walkthrough: Notes are the musical letters A to G; any pair could fit, so the word for calm has to come first.
explanation.definitionFit: A serenade is a piece of music, often sung to a lover.

clue.text: Better than expected? Certainly not at Sunningdale!

blocks.note: the everyday sense: exceeding the normal standard
on a golf course, taking more strokes than the standard is a bad score

explanation.surface: Someone says a result beat expectations, then adds that it didn't at the golf club.
explanation.walkthrough: Sunningdale is a famous golf club in Berkshire; in golf, a score above par is bad, the opposite of the everyday sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: par is the standard or expected level, so being over it means doing better than expected.

clue.text: Artless acts in North America with which this writer’s linked?

explanation.surface: An author admits to being connected with some clumsy doings in North America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This writer's' is 'this writer has', so I'VE, not a possessive.
explanation.definitionFit: Naiveties are acts showing a lack of guile, artless acts.

clue.text: Image-building included in course taken by new European tycoon

indicators.note: the image-building goes inside the course
the course is followed by new European

blocks.note: an entrée, a course of a meal

explanation.surface: A European business magnate takes a PR course.
explanation.walkthrough: Course looks like a class of study; it is a course of a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Near synonym: a tycoon is a wealthy businessperson, and the answer names someone who builds businesses.

clue.text: Account with great weight and beauty read out in Anne Brönte’s name

explanation.surface: A report that a hefty, beautiful account was read aloud under Anne Brontë's name.
explanation.walkthrough: Acton Bell was the pen name Anne Brontë wrote under, alongside Currer and Ellis Bell.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: this was the male pseudonym under which Anne Brontë published Agnes Grey.

clue.text: Scots head supporting a role in discriminatory system

indicators.note: in a down clue, the head sits below and holds up the rest

explanation.surface: A Scottish headteacher backs someone playing a part in an unfair system.
explanation.walkthrough: Apartheid was South Africa's system of racial segregation.
explanation.definitionFit: Apartheid was a system of racial discrimination in South Africa.

clue.text: Surpassed in guile — by a Murdoch company?

blocks.note: beaten by someone craftier, the fox being the emblem of cunning
Fox is the TV network Rupert Murdoch built, so the word also reads as beaten by Fox

explanation.surface: A rival asks if it was a Murdoch firm that out-schemed them.
explanation.walkthrough: Fox is the broadcaster Rupert Murdoch owns, so the jokey reading is being outdone by Fox.
explanation.definitionFit: To be outfoxed is to be beaten by someone more cunning.

clue.text: Room for experimentation involving maiden as Easter sacrifice?

indicators.note: the room takes in the maiden

explanation.surface: A lab experiment that sacrifices a young woman at Easter.
explanation.walkthrough: The lamb recalls the Passover lamb and Christ as the Lamb of God.
explanation.definitionFit: Christian symbolism: the Passover lamb and Christ as the Lamb of God make the lamb the Easter sacrifice.

clue.text: Resentment of female living in the Fens?

blocks.note: the sour feeling of having been wronged
a bittern, a wading bird of the Fens, with the feminine -ESS

explanation.surface: A complaint about the resentment of a woman who lives in the Fens.
explanation.walkthrough: The Fens are marshland in eastern England, home of the bittern; the second reading invents a female bittern, as lion gives lioness.
explanation.definitionFit: Resentment is a sour, bitter feeling, while the jokey second reading adds the feminine -ess to a Fenland heron.

clue.text: Priam’s city under-represented in particular view of the past

indicators.note: the city is not fully shown, losing its last letter
it goes inside the particular

blocks.note: in this respect = in this particular

explanation.surface: A detailed historical look at Troy that gives the city too little weight.
explanation.walkthrough: Priam was King of Troy in the Iliad.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: 'in retrospect' means looking back, and the noun is that backward look.

clue.text: Run to avoid large snake

blocks.note: a ladder is a run in tights or stockings

explanation.surface: An instruction to run away from a big snake.
explanation.walkthrough: A ladder in British English is a run in tights.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by category: the adder is Britain's only native venomous snake.

clue.text: Wager involving question put to everyone after second-rate game

indicators.note: the wager takes in the question
everyone comes after second-rate

explanation.surface: A bet on a quiz question for everyone after a mediocre match.
explanation.walkthrough: Second-rate is B, the grade below A; 'put to' is only glue between question and everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by category: a team sport played with a ball and a raised hoop is one kind of game.

clue.text: Jazz musician‘s American friend and lush

explanation.surface: A jazz player's American pal is a drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: Lush suggests a drunkard, fitting a jazz-club scene; it is the adjective meaning rich.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: he was a celebrated American big-band drummer, one jazz musician among many.

clue.text: Dramatist on vacation taking in legendary show

indicators.note: the dramatist is emptied, leaving only its outer letters
those letters hold the legendary word

explanation.surface: A playwright on holiday takes in a show about legends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Show' looks like a noun for the theatre; it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: to represent something in a picture or in words is to show it.

clue.text: Where batter needs to stand to rise?

blocks.note: a cricket batsman is safe only behind the line marked on the pitch, read as two words
a noun, as in a rise in prices

explanation.surface: A question about where cake batter should sit to rise.
explanation.walkthrough: Batter looks like cake mix that rises; it is a batsman. The crease is the line in cricket the batsman stands behind to be safe.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym, both as nouns: a pay rise is a pay increase.

clue.text: Athens ruinously allows in obtrusively religious actor

indicators.note: Athens is wrecked into a new order
the rearranged letters let the religious word inside

explanation.surface: Athens, falling to ruin, lets in a sanctimonious actor.
explanation.walkthrough: Thespis of Attica is said to be the first actor, so the Athens surface fits.
explanation.definitionFit: From Thespis, said to be the first Greek actor, the word is a slightly playful name for any actor.

clue.text: Selected comments from lawyer at last admitted to bar?

indicators.note: 'at last' means finally, so only the final letter of lawyer is used
that letter goes inside the word for bar

blocks.note: bar = except, as in 'all bar one'

explanation.surface: Quotes from a lawyer who has finally been called to the bar.
explanation.walkthrough: Being admitted to the bar is qualifying as a barrister, but bar here is the preposition meaning except.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a passage chosen from a longer text or speech is a set of selected comments.

clue.text: Romanian garden potentially yields fruit

indicators.note: the letters could be rearranged into something else

explanation.surface: A Romanian garden might produce fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is almost literal: a garden yielding fruit, and the fruit is what its letters become.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by category: a small, loose-skinned citrus is one kind of fruit.

clue.text: Seemingly wanting meal from bar in Heaven

indicators.note: the bar goes inside heaven

blocks.note: an inn, a place to drink

explanation.surface: Someone apparently hungry gets food from a heavenly bar.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition describes a look: someone skinny appears to be short of meals.
explanation.definitionFit: A skinny person looks as if they need a meal.

clue.text: Goon, Mad Dan, old fool making pastry

blocks.note: Eccles, the Goon Show character, called Mad Dan Eccles
cake is an old word for a fool

explanation.surface: A list of three idiots who together make a pastry.
explanation.walkthrough: The Goon Show was a 1950s BBC radio comedy; Eccles was its dim-witted character. An Eccles cake is a currant pastry from Lancashire.
explanation.definitionFit: An Eccles cake is a flaky pastry filled with currants.

clue.text: Old European’s say-so left Brunei reeling

indicators.note: the letters stagger into a new order

explanation.surface: An elderly European's command leaves Brunei staggering.
explanation.walkthrough: Byelorussia is the old name for Belarus, which is why the European is 'old'.
explanation.definitionFit: A Byelorussian is a person from Byelorussia, the former name of Belarus.

clue.text: Solitary individual such as Shylock, did you say?

indicators.note: the word is heard, not seen

blocks.note: Shylock is the moneylender in The Merchant of Venice, one who loans

explanation.surface: Asking whether Shylock was a solitary figure.
explanation.walkthrough: Shylock is the moneylender in Shakespeare's The Merchant of Venice, and he did end up isolated, so the surface is apt.
explanation.definitionFit: A loner is someone who prefers to be alone.

clue.text: Suffer as a result of hot dog that’s rather unpleasant

blocks.note: a cur is a nasty mongrel

explanation.surface: Someone pays the price for a nasty hot dog.
explanation.walkthrough: Hot dog reads as the snack; hot is IN, as in fashionable, and the dog is the cur.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: to bring a cost or penalty on yourself is to suffer it as a result of your actions.

clue.text: Rude wife showed the way to guards

indicators.note: the word for showed the way surrounds the wife

explanation.surface: A crude wife led the way to the sentries.
explanation.walkthrough: Guards looks like a noun for sentries, which 'to' supports; it is the verb, holding W.
explanation.definitionFit: Lewd means rude in the crude, sexual sense.

clue.text: Elegy dreadful, Gray initially admitted

indicators.note: 'initially' means at the start, so only Gray's first letter is used
the letter is let into dreadful

explanation.surface: Thomas Gray confesses that his elegy is dreadful.
explanation.walkthrough: Gray wrote the famous Elegy Written in a Country Churchyard, so the surface is literary gossip.
explanation.definitionFit: Near synonym: a mournful funeral song and a poem lamenting the dead are both laments.

clue.text: Desperate character, northern drunk lying about winemaker?

indicators.note: the northern drunk is turned around

blocks.note: Desperate Dan, the strongman of the Dandy comic

explanation.surface: A desperate northern drunk sprawled around a vintner.
explanation.walkthrough: Desperate Dan is a British comic-strip character. The question mark marks the whimsical definition: dandelions are made into wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Dandelion flowers are used to make country wine.

clue.text: Advanced study almost containing 100 insights

indicators.note: the study loses its last letter
to contain is to hold within, so the shortened study holds the 100

blocks.note: A = advanced, as in A level

explanation.surface: Advanced study, nearly finished, yields a hundred insights.
explanation.walkthrough: An aperçu is a French-derived word for a brief illuminating comment.
explanation.definitionFit: Loanword: from French for 'glimpsed', these are brief illuminating comments or insights.

clue.text: Gullible Romeo has waited, drinking whisky, outside

indicators.note: the word for waited takes in the whisky
it also sits outside Romeo

blocks.note: Romeo is R in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: A naive Romeo hung about outside, drinking whisky.
explanation.walkthrough: Romeo reads as the lover waiting under a balcony; it is only the letter R.
explanation.definitionFit: Starry-eyed means naively idealistic, gullible.

clue.text: Sprinter runs to get hold of singlet one gathers

indicators.note: the sprinter and runs grip the singlet between them

blocks.note: a hare is a fast runner

explanation.surface: A sprinter races to grab a running vest that someone collects.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One gathers' sounds like 'I gather', but it defines: a harvester is one who gathers crops.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by description: whether person or machine, it is the one that gathers in the crops.
